A red wine headache is a headache that develops quickly—often within 30 minutes to three hours—after drinking even a small amount of red wine, distinct from a typical hangover . Researchers suspect a plant compound called **quercetin** in red grape skins may block alcohol metabolism, though the exact cause is still being studied.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF11iRhhDBCpMkRhweKiWrOtQvgzStIrSpM1LclyNSj1-JLPSebxUdJZX2wi8WbHG1oYfRKDADnHxuavXqYcZG-OP2_0xQfLI4HvWpjUu0955H5o6pT1W3T-sUqLEr8NzMfwTWqTRqgYP1y5X4_7xsoLGq82ms7SEVwMkP_7SzSJvFP-AuoVlAMaT_Sg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXqbMjtobdgUqzugQatlcV96S96HjjOy8POssdab06g_aDZaou4XB6sdOkTQmvT5sBWOEmqNS19Nn_xXwNkVeDc07zHOTrbkG2VLo05-Jdxyj6XPnzXcFtf8B1-tBDYdRlFTkfjVhO4Ac)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXZJiBXQWy4Wnh0fmtQVTtRT7c2KX_k-CnmD2ESrBPai_p6xqgqk3etiepQ0L3oQIrA9BIfFLsfTEYN9RgemDKPGyV2pwNTs0L2cpcHkIIr_X9IaKTsc3yFM5pU9cCtMCDET4YpDI)

### What Causes It

- **Quercetin and acetaldehyde:** Quercetin (a flavanol abundant in sun-exposed red grapes) may inhibit the enzyme that breaks down acetaldehyde, an alcohol byproduct that can trigger headaches and inflammation when it builds up.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zyZyJZLwUxPkzBWYT_r_mkiRj-fE_fyJ87TEhZ-614ipZ9oDyu4IlEq-4oS6u8lYrnDdqHigY066RDzh-GvjX31M4oPerLBulke3V9_BE6LZp6qBytBbEkjQHxYRvmcYTjMmid6DAUdR9LCcYX21xQrsx3-czNIZ5GSLgtGlc0yqnLC)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkAEBxCJF14EijyecptrOxAaNN11b0856W_MDCRItoN1JiLykSCq6H6BpKSyFCjQ2C_PYIEDAFYBWKwzqskCHflSmnxeqoPsXEvk7qBmIs8hcAWGEOmMNzP1IhE5C3I8qhmDYKRq9p4-O6k3lUVjEyLsThSiZZO4P1d0MtZDLIkHyonUEhgQZOXDGvQjCXuVuBEw)
- **Other proposed culprits:** Sulfites, histamines, and tannins are often blamed, though evidence is mixed. For example, white wines and dried fruits often contain sulfites without reliably causing the same reaction.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXK0b2zXKeX3nocE1NXC_eyG3e5MJ-C-Y07QZiruJvUuAQRt8QUdmiCecL4uT79lvH92JFTRHLJ5FYcbiPiZSH-GvgIA83y5-2ywJZ2R9kuuqAfeSiaQZ8ka21hU-0ZzT_eRy4R90)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1wPU-svY2fVMjeAw0Y57VO7BP2UEdroCqHJNqqP67EuTFgSuEBeHs-WqHUCAWHwNOaR4Enk2zW64px-rDeaT0yxy-qmPBm_I89O5090xBj_4bku5kZ6NAUw2T7GmzZ9QYe7d03ULRkjx7BR82s0gtxv3mh2hi-zSalbiENIvB9A)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXc16l9MUBspCCaqL_z8DfST_PEnvVIbJ0EQF8Sf5OZKlqryDVUHtYd8CI-gH5F1oLiX7OHEsdhlAqUreyC-geiT0Yti3GmFn58Onf_M8dxxBWKg0-8QBrJVCD968YmOKfEg)

### Symptoms, Duration, and Risk Factors

- **Symptoms:** Throbbing or pounding head pain, sometimes accompanied by facial flushing, sweating, or nausea.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXVawCv3vH3cEiaJYrUHCriwT6ZOw8hI-5B9T5ghKSOm6PQpAGlkepIAIhOlrTdOJEU4_DaRKnQaeYLYw5n27nEdtM-eYzauYwiDTBnMlyX3fSImEHwMnqpIupwXmQOMvT)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXQ-lnd3uewWMSxxX1pV3_ztIO_d27YnU1GIhzazrMFPj7Lf1dB1qnK7V7ddfv5rmnCJ-GEMv3R0HlGPTwsy_frlCXZM0nX2dpJ6WTMHeDsxNsJnJQGehp-INVjkBllOmlmg)
- **Onset and duration:** Typically starts within 30 minutes to three hours of drinking and generally resolves within 72 hours after stopping alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXqbMjtobdgUqzugQatlcV96S96HjjOy8POssdab06g_aDZaou4XB6sdOkTQmvT5sBWOEmqNS19Nn_xXwNkVeDc07zHOTrbkG2VLo05-Jdxyj6XPnzXcFtf8B1-tBDYdRlFTkfjVhO4Ac)
- **Risk factors:** People prone to migraines or those with variations in alcohol-metabolizing enzymes (such as ALDH2) may be more susceptible.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF1zyZyJZLwUxPkzBWYT_r_mkiRj-fE_fyJ87TEhZ-614ipZ9oDyu4IlEq-4oS6u8lYrnDdqHigY066RDzh-GvjX31M4oPerLBulke3V9_BE6LZp6qBytBbEkjQHxYRvmcYTjMmid6DAUdR9LCcYX21xQrsx3-czNIZ5GSLgtGlc0yqnLC)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXqbMjtobdgUqzugQatlcV96S96HjjOy8POssdab06g_aDZaou4XB6sdOkTQmvT5sBWOEmqNS19Nn_xXwNkVeDc07zHOTrbkG2VLo05-Jdxyj6XPnzXcFtf8B1-tBDYdRlFTkfjVhO4Ac)

### Prevention and Treatment

- **Switch drinks:** White or rosé wines generally have lower quercetin levels than red wine.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)
- **Eat and hydrate:** Have a full meal before drinking and drink water alongside or after wine.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF11iRhhDBCpMkRhweKiWrOtQvgzStIrSpM1LclyNSj1-JLPSebxUdJZX2wi8WbHG1oYfRKDADnHxuavXqYcZG-OP2_0xQfLI4HvWpjUu0955H5o6pT1W3T-sUqLEr8NzMfwTWqTRqgYP1y5X4_7xsoLGq82ms7SEVwMkP_7SzSJvFP-AuoVlAMaT_Sg)
- **Track specific wines:** Quercetin levels vary by grape exposure and winemaking, and are not listed on labels, so noting which bottles trigger symptoms can help.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXVawCv3vH3cEiaJYrUHCriwT6ZOw8hI-5B9T5ghKSOm6PQpAGlkepIAIhOlrTdOJEU4_DaRKnQaeYLYw5n27nEdtM-eYzauYwiDTBnMlyX3fSImEHwMnqpIupwXmQOMvT)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXQ-lnd3uewWMSxxX1pV3_ztIO_d27YnU1GIhzazrMFPj7Lf1dB1qnK7V7ddfv5rmnCJ-GEMv3R0HlGPTwsy_frlCXZM0nX2dpJ6WTMHeDsxNsJnJQGehp-INVjkBllOmlmg)
- **Treating a headache:** Rest and hydration can help. Using over-the-counter pain relievers with alcohol carries risks—such as stomach irritation or liver strain—so check with a doctor or pharmacist first, and see a headache specialist if headaches are frequent.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmAEBxCJF134QJYMV8ZGAEV9d9ShIGJbBLwXGK8nCTPdBw8VjM6b4iW8FWVkvPLSCdx-OkJIWhNjYDn0XHo9Uiiz1ZN613OxWGGQZcO2ZhzA_QmvhrMvFnqgjIQx5iJ339kKHigJbBXvTxeaviUGabTi4Rul7B-kIogKcUq4WjluwG77GH2Rz7VNinZ61Aban7Nwab42lGXsfbA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXVawCv3vH3cEiaJYrUHCriwT6ZOw8hI-5B9T5ghKSOm6PQpAGlkepIAIhOlrTdOJEU4_DaRKnQaeYLYw5n27nEdtM-eYzauYwiDTBnMlyX3fSImEHwMnqpIupwXmQOMvT)

For more details, see [Harvard Health](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF11iRhhDBCpMkRhweKiWrOtQvgzStIrSpM1LclyNSj1-JLPSebxUdJZX2wi8WbHG1oYfRKDADnHxuavXqYcZG-OP2_0xQfLI4HvWpjUu0955H5o6pT1W3T-sUqLEr8NzMfwTWqTRqgYP1y5X4_7xsoLGq82ms7SEVwMkP_7SzSJvFP-AuoVlAMaT_Sg) or the [Red wine headache](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXK0b2zXKeX3nocE1NXC_eyG3e5MJ-C-Y07QZiruJvUuAQRt8QUdmiCecL4uT79lvH92JFTRHLJ5FYcbiPiZSH-GvgIA83y5-2ywJZ2R9kuuqAfeSiaQZ8ka21hU-0ZzT_eRy4R90) overview.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXK0b2zXKeX3nocE1NXC_eyG3e5MJ-C-Y07QZiruJvUuAQRt8QUdmiCecL4uT79lvH92JFTRHLJ5FYcbiPiZSH-GvgIA83y5-2ywJZ2R9kuuqAfeSiaQZ8ka21hU-0ZzT_eRy4R90)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjwEBxCJF11iRhhDBCpMkRhweKiWrOtQvgzStIrSpM1LclyNSj1-JLPSebxUdJZX2wi8WbHG1oYfRKDADnHxuavXqYcZG-OP2_0xQfLI4HvWpjUu0955H5o6pT1W3T-sUqLEr8NzMfwTWqTRqgYP1y5X4_7xsoLGq82ms7SEVwMkP_7SzSJvFP-AuoVlAMaT_Sg)Are you looking into this for yourself or someone else, and would you like to explore **prevention tips**, **how it compares to migraines** , or **when to see a doctor**?

items.title: Prevention and Treatment
items.text: Switch drinks: White or rosé wines generally have lower quercetin levels than red wine. Eat and hydrate: Have a full meal before drinking and drink water alongside or after wine. Track specific wines: Quercetin levels vary by grape exposure and winemaking, and are not listed on labels, so noting which bottles trigger symptoms can help. Treating a headache: Rest and hydration can help. Using over-the-counter pain relievers with alcohol carries risks—such as stomach irritation or liver strain—so check with a doctor or pharmacist first, and see a headache specialist if headaches are frequent.
